chapter_theme: The sun of the mind (மன ஆதித்தன்): sun, moon and fire are taken as the lights and breaths within. When the two rays become one the life-breath stops wandering and the clear-minded become Siva; beyond these lights shines one that the bounded cannot perceive, and without the First One's grace there is only darkness.

1988.reading: As the glittering dew melts before the darting rays of the sun and the moon shines facing it, my life-breath, moving within the spreading rays, will stop wandering once it becomes a single ray.
1988.nuance: Sun and moon are traditionally the right and left breaths (pingala and ida), and the 'single ray' their union in the central channel. ஆவி may be breath or life; உலாஅது is 'will not roam'. A plain reading of dawn and moonlight also stands, but the last two lines push toward the yogic one.

1989.reading: Worship when moon and sun come together, in the way the moon comes to meet the sun that went before; those whose minds grow clear in the place of the two become Siva.
1989.nuance: பானு (sun) and இந்து (moon) may be the new-moon conjunction or, as tradition takes it, the two breaths meeting. உபய நிலம் ('the ground of both') is commonly placed between the brows or in the central channel; the verse does not say where.

1990.reading: Sun, fire and moon come with their kalas, and between the kalas, they say, there are four; know that when the sun joins fire and moon, that is the fullness.
1990.nuance: அருக்கன் அனல் மதி are the three lights, traditionally matched with three breaths or regions of the body. What the 'four' between the kalas are is not stated. பூரணை is the full moon and, figuratively, fullness or completion.

1991.reading: That light which moves beyond the two spheres is an awareness that those of a single sphere cannot perceive; it stands shining through the great sphere, and only those fit to approach it are fit to know it.
1991.nuance: அண்டம் is the cosmic egg or world-sphere; ஈர் அண்டம், ஓர் அண்டம் and பேர் அண்டம் are not explained and may be read cosmically or of regions in the body. The last line plays on அண்டு (approach) and அண்டம் (sphere).

1992.reading: Dwelling in the nine it circles the world, yet no one knows the nature of the Lord in the nine; those who dwelt in it before but lack the First One's grace are without bliss and stand surrounded by darkness.
1992.nuance: ஒன்பது is unexplained: the nine planets that circle the world fit the chapter's suns and moons, and the body's nine gates are another traditional reading. The contrast between dwelling in it and having grace is the clear point.

source_issues: 1988 line 1: மின்பனி may be மின் பனி (glittering dew) or a corruption; the sense of சோரும் (droops, melts) is clear.
